name: 5 Card Stud High-Low With a Buy
description: Five Card Stud High-Low with a Buy: each player gets one hole card and four face-up cards over four betting rounds. Pot split between best high hand and best low hand (typically 8-or-better). The buy is an optional mechanic allowing players to purchase an extra card or modifier; exact implementation varies by house rules.
alsoKnownAs: Five Card Stud High-Low With a Buy Poker

overview.description: Five Card Stud High-Low with a Buy: each player gets one hole card and four face-up cards over four betting rounds. Pot split between best high hand and best low hand (typically 8-or-better). The buy is an optional mechanic allowing players to purchase an extra card or modifier; exact implementation varies by house rules.

history.origins: Stud poker first appeared in America in the 1860s as an open game with one hole card and four face-up cards. Five Card Stud High-Low with a Buy is a home and club variant that combines the high-low split pot with an optional buy round after the fifth card; it persists in home games even as casino five-card stud declined in the late 20th century.
timeline: 1860s: Stud poker appears in America as an open game with one down and four up cards.
20th century: Home and club games experiment with five-card stud high-low split pots.
Late 20th century: High-low stud with a buy persists as a home and club variant even as casino five-card stud declines.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack. Only five cards per player are dealt, so up to 10 can play.
setup.dealing: One down, four up; four betting rounds.

rules.objective: Win high half and or low half of pot (8-or-better for low). Buy: optional extra card or modifier per house rules.
rules.gameplay: Ante; one card down, one up. Bet; three more up cards with betting. Showdown: best high and best qualifying low split.

strategy.basic: Play for both ways when possible.
strategy.intermediate: Read board for scoop potential; fold weak one-way hands.
strategy.advanced: Buy timing and sizing; table-stakes implications.
tips: Qualify low (8-or-better); buy rules are house-specific.

variations.name: Two rounds of buying
variations.description: After the fifth card, play two buy rounds; the second round costs more (e.g. two large bets) than the first.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variant only changes how many buy rounds are offered and how expensive they are; engine overrides for these parameters are not yet modeled.

scoring.winCondition: Win high half and or low half of pot (8-or-better for low). Buy: optional extra card or modifier per house rules.
